acceptance.criterion: Hub Ask distinguishes local request throttling from provider quota, credential, permission, model-access, and configuration failures without exposing provider response bodies or credentials.
acceptance.notes: Tests cover OpenAI insufficient-quota classification and true provider rate limiting with Retry-After propagation; 12 Hub advisor tests and Ruff pass.

activities.title: Test a deployment candidate and share feedback
activities.implementation_notes: Jira remains the feedback and announcement record; its Software board configuration, issue statuses, priorities, transitions, comments and project property drive the platform UI. Testers choose a plain-language intent before composing; intent is stored in the Jira property and label. Completed feedback stays compact but is promoted for tester confirmation: Looks good closes or hides it, while Still happening returns it to the board's first open column. GitHub merge messages and explicit release notes drive candidate updates. Existing user details store bounded per-user read receipts. Submitted descriptions are immutable and reproduction context is server-sanitized.
activities.group_title: Measure, govern, and operate the platform

acceptance.criterion: Authenticated users on an unstable build see a full-width banner outside the normal layout, unread counts for announcements, merge updates, and feedback, and responsive anchored panels or a phone bottom tray.
acceptance.notes: Browser UI verification explicitly deferred by the product owner on 2026-09-11; source compiles and lints, but no layout claim is recorded.

acceptance.criterion: Testers can send an immutable note with up to three images and privacy-sanitized reproduction context, revisit only their own Jira-backed submissions, and append follow-up comments.
acceptance.notes: Focused API tests verify sanitization, ownership-scoped serialization and absence of the edit endpoint; TypeScript validates the append-only client contract.

acceptance.criterion: Platform operators can publish tester announcements and manage feedback through Jira board columns, native priorities and available transitions, with explicit shared replies and separate internal notes.
acceptance.notes: Focused API tests verify live Jira board-column mapping and comment audiences; platform UI and service contracts compile and lint.

acceptance.criterion: Internal notes, other users feedback, private route values, full user-agent strings, and other personally owned reproduction data are not disclosed or captured.
acceptance.notes: Focused API tests verify internal-note exclusion, user ownership filtering, dynamic route redaction, reduced browser/platform families and malformed-context handling.

acceptance.criterion: Testers see human-authored merge messages instead of technical commit subjects, and completed feedback shows when Jira moved it to Done.
acceptance.notes: Focused API tests verify technical commit subjects are omitted, explicit/merge notes are retained, and Jira Done category changes serialize a completion timestamp.

acceptance.criterion: The feedback panel begins with plain-language intents plus a freeform path, keeps submission history compact, promotes completed items needing review, and lets a tester close a resolved item or return it to the board's first open column.
acceptance.notes: Focused API tests cover intent persistence and reopening completed feedback; TypeScript and focused ESLint validate the intent-first composer and compact completion-review client. Browser interaction verification is owner-deferred.

steps.title: Review candidate announcements and merge updates
steps.description: See unread badges, receive oldest-first announcement prompts, and review human-authored merge notes with per-user read receipts.
steps.implementation_notes: The full-width candidate banner owns all three unread streams. Announcements use per-item receipts; release notes use the deployed revision. The candidate root, backdrop, panels, toolbar, and full Hub frame use shared layering plus shrinkable dynamic-viewport bounds so opening a panel does not widen or displace the application.

references.responsibility: Read curated GitHub release notes for deployed revisions.
Render the full-width banner, automatic announcement sequence, anchored desktop panels, and phone tray.
Present unseen notes above earlier updates.
Release-note parsing and unread grouping checks.

steps.title: Submit and continue candidate feedback
steps.description: Choose a feedback intent or Something else, send an immutable note with screenshots and sanitized reproduction context, then review owned submissions, append follow-ups, and confirm or reopen completed work.
steps.implementation_notes: The focused composer starts with five color-and-icon intent choices in a two-column grid plus a freeform path, then places Back and Send around the intent-specific prompt and briefly confirms submission. Jira descriptions remain immutable. Activity-sorted history stays one line until expanded, exposes authenticated image thumbnails and shared comments, marks unread activity, and keeps completed-item resolution actions at the bottom.

references.responsibility: Authorize feedback creation, edits, history, confirmation, and attachments.
Quick feedback composer, screenshots, history, replies, and confirmation.
Desktop and phone tester interaction checks.

steps.title: Operate platform tester feedback
steps.description: Publish announcements and manage feedback in Superadmin using the Jira board columns, priorities, transitions, internal notes, and explicitly tester-visible replies.
steps.implementation_notes: The application keeps no shadow feedback workflow. Per-user feedback receipts compare the Jira status and latest shared team reply while ignoring internal and tester-authored comments.

verification.evidence: BOT-210 API tests cover Jira board-column mapping and tester/internal/shared comment visibility; TypeScript, focused ESLint and routing tests pass. Live Jira and browser administration checks remain owner-deferred/manual.

references.responsibility: Map application actions to Jira issues, attachments, comments, priorities, and workflow.
Expose feedback and announcement operations within platform administration.
Outstanding feedback triage, communication, and fix handoff.
Desktop and phone administrator triage checks.
